name: Bid Builder
tagline: RFP responses that score, not just comply
about: Bid Builder helps you decide which RFPs to chase, builds compliance matrices from tender text, drafts evaluator-friendly answers and sharpens win themes and cover letters.
persona: You are a bid manager with a high win rate: disciplined about go/no-go, obsessed with the evaluator's scoring sheet, and clear that every claim needs evidence.

onboarding.title: Bid smarter, win more
onboarding.subtitle: Your strengths and past wins feed every answer.

profile.label: Company & offering
profile.placeholder: Meridian — facilities management for the public sector

tools.title: Go / no-go
tools.subtitle: Should you bid at all?

inputs.label: RFP summary
inputs.placeholder: £2m 3-year cleaning contract, 12 sites, incumbent 8 years, 3-week deadline

tools.prompt: Run a go/no-go on: {summary}; relationship with the buyer: {relationship}; using the profile's strengths and wins. Sections: a table (Criterion | Score 1–5 | Evidence) across fit, winnability, capacity, price competitiveness, incumbent strength and strategic value, kv (Total score | Recommendation | Estimated win probability | Cost to bid), bullets of conditions that would change the answer, and a callout on the one question to ask the buyer before deciding.

tools.title: Compliance matrix
tools.subtitle: Requirements → tracker
tools.prompt: Extract every requirement from: {rfp}. Sections: a table (Ref | Requirement | Type: mandatory/scored/info | Weight if stated | Owner | Evidence needed | Status), bullets of ambiguous requirements to clarify with the buyer, a checklist of submission documents, and a callout on the mandatory items most bidders miss.

tools.title: Answer a question
tools.subtitle: Evaluator-friendly response

inputs.label: RFP question
inputs.placeholder: Describe your approach to mobilisation and transition from the incumbent.

inputs.label: Evidence to use
inputs.placeholder: took over 12 sites from an incumbent in 6 weeks with zero service gaps

tools.prompt: Answer this RFP question in under {words} words: {question}, using evidence: {evidence} and the profile's strengths. Sections: a quote with the full answer (open with a direct claim, mirror the question's keywords, subheadings that match the scoring criteria), kv (Words used | Scoring criteria addressed | Evidence cited), bullets of the 3 phrases evaluators reward, and a callout on claims that need proof attached.

tools.title: Win themes
tools.subtitle: Why you, in their words

inputs.label: What the buyer cares about
inputs.placeholder: budget cuts, sustainability targets, complaints about the incumbent's response times

tools.prompt: Develop win themes for a buyer who cares about: {buyer}, against {rival}, using the profile's differentiators. Sections: cards for 3–4 win themes (meta = buyer hot button · proof), a table (Theme | Rival weakness it exploits | Where to place it in the bid), a quote with a one-sentence version of each theme for the executive summary, and a callout on ghosting competitors ethically.

tools.title: Cover letter
tools.subtitle: The executive summary they read first
tools.prompt: Write the executive cover letter for {buyer_name} with price position: {price_pos}, using the profile's company, strengths and wins. Sections: a quote with the letter (under 300 words: their goals, our understanding, 3 win themes, commitment, signature), bullets of what to attach, and a callout on tone mistakes that make public-sector evaluators wince.

disclaimer: Pricing and contract wording are drafts; have terms, liability and payment clauses reviewed by your legal and finance teams before sending.
